events.body:
## Bug

`website/utils.py:294` — `safe_redirect_allowed(url, allowed_hosts, allowed_paths)` calls `is_safe_url(...)`, but `is_safe_url` is never imported or defined in the module (no import, no star-import). Every call raises `NameError: name 'is_safe_url' is not defined`.

This function is the open-redirect guard: it is meant to validate `url` before `redirect(...)`. With the guard itself crashing, any redirect routed through it fails, and a caller that wraps it in a broad `except` could fail open.

## Why the name is missing

Django removed `django.utils.http.is_safe_url` in Django 4.0 (renamed to `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`, with a different signature). This is leftover from a Django upgrade.

## Repro

Call `safe_redirect_allowed("https://evil.example/", {"legacy.owaspblt.org"})` → `NameError`.

## Suggested fix

Use the current API instead of re-adding the removed name:

    from django.utils.http import url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme
    ...
    if url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme(url, allowed_hosts=allowed_hosts):

(and adapt the `allowed_paths` handling accordingly).

Found by static analysis (ruff F821); confirmed no import or definition exists in the module. AI model used in analysis: Claude Opus 4.8 (Claude Code).
